review_defects.claim_says: The conditions imported from the Cotton Textile approval are incorporated as they stood and add no end of their own; no held record shows an earlier end, so the first end is 1935-06-14.
review_defects.source_says: Held EO 6206 (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6206-code-fair-competition-for-the-cotton-textile-industry.txt, July 16, 1933) records that the Cotton Textile approval of July 9, 1933 carried 'condition 12 of said order providing for the termination of approval at the end of four months unless expressly renewed', withdrawn only on July 16, 1933 and only for the Cotton Textile code. EO 6204-A (July 14, 1933) approved the Rayon Weaving provisions 'subject to the interpretations and conditions imposed by me on my approval of the corresponding provisions of said Cotton Textile Code', so as they stood on July 14 the imported conditions included a four-month termination. The claim neither addresses this possible own-terms end (about November 1933, unless renewed or unless the July 16 withdrawal carried over) nor records it as a gap.

review_defects.source_says: Whether the imported four-month termination condition applied to this partial approval, and whether any renewal or later Rayon Weaving action followed (the July 9 order and any renewal are not held), is a material open question on the first end. The parallel partial approval of the Throwing Industry the same day (EO 6204-B) was followed by a full approval (EO 6331-E, WPA p. 543), which shows interim approvals of this form were superseded; for Rayon Weaving none is held, which is absence of evidence, not proof.

review_defects.claim_says: The single clause, defined to include the naming sentence ('This reservation shall be known as the Minnewastena Migratory Waterfowl Refuge'), ended on 1958-08-05; the only later event is Reorganization Plan No. II; 'No earlier named instrument ... was found'.
review_defects.source_says: Proclamation No. 2416, 'Changing the Names of Certain Federal Wildlife Refuges', signed July 25, 1940, filed July 27, 1940, 5 FR 2677-2680 (Federal Register of July 30, 1940), held in the FR text layer jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_8494.txt (sha256 87e6c363552ebc78ddc3b93a269adfe3752ef2d318a06f44831141791d006bb8; also EO_8496.txt): 'do proclaim that the names of the Federal wildlife refuges listed below are hereby changed as indicated', with the old-name column listing 'Minnewastena Migratory Waterfowl Refuge' and the new-name column 'Minnewastena National Wildlife Refuge'. A held presidential instrument that names this refuge changed the name this order prescribed on July 25, 1940, eighteen years before PLO 1704. The claim omits this later event and states that the naming command ended in 1958; the searches were by order number only and could not find a renaming by refuge name.

review_defects.claim_says: The single clause, which includes the naming sentence ('This reservation shall be known as the Pioneer Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge'), ended on 1958-08-05 by Public Land Order 1704. The only later event is Reorganization Plan No. II, and no earlier named instrument was found.
review_defects.source_says: Proclamation No. 2416, 'Changing the Names of Certain Federal Wildlife Refuges', was signed July 25, 1940, filed July 27, 1940, and printed at 5 FR 2677-2680 (Federal Register of July 30, 1940). Its held FR text layer is jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_8494.txt (sha256 87e6c363552ebc78ddc3b93a269adfe3752ef2d318a06f44831141791d006bb8; also EO_8496.txt). It says: 'do proclaim that the names of the Federal wildlife refuges listed below are hereby changed as indicated'. The old-name column lists 'Pioneer Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge' and the new-name column lists 'Pioneer Lake National Wildlife Refuge'. This held presidential act names the refuge and replaced the order's naming command 18 years before PLO 1704. The claim omits it.

A held source, jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12344.txt (OFR editorial note), states that the Community Services Administration was abolished by Pub. L. 97-35 (1981).
